title: A Train Station Stayed Open for Just One Girl 🚉 #shorts
cast: a Japanese high school girl in a navy school uniform with a school bag

lines.say: In Japan, a railway kept a station open for years, just for one passenger.
shots: a tiny wooden train station in snowy countryside, a single girl waiting
close-up of {hero} smiling with a scarf, snow falling

lines.say: Kami Shirataki station was in a quiet corner of Hokkaido. Hardly anyone used it any more.
shots: a lonely railway platform among snowy pine forests
an old station sign covered in snow, no readable text

lines.say: The railway company planned to close it. But they noticed one regular passenger.
shots: office workers looking at a train timetable on a wall
a small train arriving at the empty station

lines.say: A high school student took the train there every day to get to school.
shots: {hero} stepping onto a one-carriage train in the morning snow
{hero} reading a book on the train by a frosty window

lines.say: So the station stayed open, with trains stopping at the times she needed them, for her school days.
shots: a train stopping only for {hero} at the platform, morning light

lines.say: In March 2016, she graduated. And the station closed, its job done.
shots: {hero} in a graduation ceremony holding a diploma tube
the empty station on its last day with flowers on the bench

lines.say: The story spread around the world as one of the kindest things a railway ever did.
shots: people around the world reading the story on phones and newspapers
a warm sunset over the old station in spring

lines.say: Would you keep a station open for one person?
shots: {hero} looking back at the station one last time
the train disappearing into the snowy forest

description:
JR Hokkaido kept Kami-Shirataki station in use until the one regular passenger, a high school student, graduated in March 2016. A true story.

Sources: Japan Times; BBC News (2016).

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
